programmes.institution: University of Edinburgh (School of Informatics, delivered by EPCC)
programmes.programme_name: MSc High Performance Computing (also PgDip; sister programmes HPC with Data Science, online HPC, Imaging Vision and HPC)
programmes.duration: MSc 1 year full-time (Sept start) or 3 years part-time; PgDip 9 months (study.ed.ac.uk). Online variant: 3-6 years part-time intermittent.
programmes.credits: 180 SCQF credits (120 taught + 60 dissertation); most courses 10 SCQF credits = 5 ECTS per course page
programmes.delivery: on-site (an online part-time intermittent version also exists)
programmes.entry_requirements: UK 2:1 honours degree or international equivalent in a relevant subject (computer science, physics, maths, engineering, biology, chemistry, geosciences); experienced programmer in at least one of C, C++, Python or Fortran; familiarity with algebra, linear algebra, probability and statistics; English-language proof.
programmes.structure_summary: Two semesters of taught courses (120 credits) then a three-month dissertation (60 credits). Compulsory: Message-Passing Programming, Threaded Programming, HPC Architectures, Practical Software Development and Project Preparation; 40-60 credits of EPCC HPC options (numerical algorithms, parallel algorithms, performance programming, accelerated systems, parallel design patterns, advanced MPI, HPC languages) plus up to 20 credits of data or outside courses (data management, ML at scale, HPDA, quantum). Dissertations can be industry-based.

programmes.notes: Study page lists 2027 entry; 2026-27 degree programme table is the latest course list. Variants: HPC with Data Science (on-campus and online), online HPC MSc (3-6 years, part-time intermittent), joint MSc Imaging, Vision and HPC with Heriot-Watt (see EPCC masters page). Optional dedicated courses counted as 2 in topic_coverage even though not compulsory (progression rule requires passing 3 of: MPI, Threaded, HPC Architectures, Parallel Design Patterns, Advanced MPI, Accelerated Systems). Syllabi of options read via course descriptors (DRPS) 2026/27; no course mentions containers, cloud, energy, resilience or observability, hence 0.
programmes.structure_summary_fr: Deux semestres de cours (120 crédits) puis un mémoire de trois mois (60 crédits). Obligatoires : Programmation par passage de messages, Programmation à threads, Architectures HPC, Développement logiciel pratique et Préparation du projet ; 40 à 60 crédits d'options HPC de l'EPCC (algorithmes numériques, algorithmes parallèles, programmation orientée performance, systèmes accélérés, motifs de conception parallèle, MPI avancé, langages HPC), plus jusqu'à 20 crédits de cours de données ou extérieurs (gestion de données, ML à grande échelle, analyse de données haute performance, quantique). Les mémoires peuvent être réalisés en entreprise.

programmes.institution: EUMaster4HPC consortium (coordinator University of Luxembourg; awarding universities UPC, Politecnico di Milano, FAU Erlangen-Nurnberg, Sorbonne, Sofia University, AGH Krakow, VSB Ostrava, FU Berlin)
programmes.programme_name: EUMaster4HPC - European Master for High Performance Computing (dual degree)
programmes.degree: MSc (dual degree from two consortium universities)
programmes.duration: 2 years (4 semesters of 30 ECTS); mobility between two countries, Year 1 at a host university and Year 2 specialisation at a visiting university
programmes.credits: 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester; thesis or internship 30 ECTS in semester 4)
programmes.entry_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a STEM subject, computer science or related field; at least two university-level CS courses (data structures, algorithms, programming); solid technical mathematics (list of at least four courses); English at CEFR B2 (TOEFL 85 or IELTS 5, or English-taught degree). Citizens of listed countries are eligible for tuition waiver and mobility scholarship.
programmes.structure_summary: Year 1 at a host university covers fundamentals (mathematics and statistics, software engineering, parallel programming, computer architecture, transversal skills). Year 2 at a different-country university offers a specialisation: Numerical and Data Specialist, Performance Analyst and Advisor, System Development and Support, or System Architect (AI and Quantum specialisations are in development). Closes with a 30 ECTS master thesis or internship. Extracurricular summer school, workshops, challenge and internships are mandatory.

programmes.notes: Consortium-level curriculum: courses are taught at the awarding universities, so coverage reflects the published curriculum areas/specialisations plus the FAU standard study plan (only course-level plan read); Luxembourg, UPC, Polimi, Sorbonne etc. course catalogues not read here. Coverage values for scheduling, ml-systems, viz, resilience and observability-sre are null (unknown). Application window for the 2026 intake closed 15 August 2026 per EuroHPC press release. Partner programmes (per awarded-degrees page): Polimi LM in HPC Engineering (120 credits, cloud infrastructures and data centres, quantum computing, GPUs and tensor cores), UPC MIRI-HPC, FU Berlin MSc Computational Sciences, Sorbonne, Sofia.
programmes.structure_summary_fr: L'année 1, dans une université d'accueil, couvre les fondamentaux (mathématiques et statistiques, génie logiciel, programmation parallèle, architecture des ordinateurs, compétences transversales). L'année 2, dans une université d'un autre pays, propose une spécialisation : spécialiste numérique et données, analyste et conseiller en performance, développement et support de systèmes, ou architecte de systèmes (des spécialisations IA et quantique sont en développement). Le cursus se termine par un mémoire ou un stage de 30 ECTS. Une école d'été, des ateliers, un défi et des stages extracurriculaires sont obligatoires.

programmes.programme_name: Master in Computational Science and Engineering (RW/CSE)
programmes.duration: 4 semesters (three semesters of courses then a six-month master thesis) under Studienreglement 2024; programme page still shows 1.5 years for the older 90 ECTS regulation
programmes.credits: 120 ECTS (Studienreglement 2024; older cohorts 90 ECTS): main areas >= 74 incl. 2 core courses (>= 12), field of specialization 18, electives; case studies 6; term project 8; science in perspective 2; thesis 30
programmes.entry_requirements: ETH RW/CSE Bachelor from D-MATH admitted directly; otherwise a Bachelor degree of at least 180 ECTS from a university, with admission by ETH procedure; students without the ETH CSE Bachelor must take extra courses (guidelines section 3.4-3.5).
programmes.structure_summary: Interdisciplinary CSE master: two core courses chosen from a list (AI in the Sciences and Engineering, Advanced Machine Learning, Advanced Numerical Methods for CSE, Probabilistic AI, Computational Statistics, Advanced Systems Lab, Optimization for Data Science), at least two fields of application (astrophysics, biology, chemistry, finance, electromagnetics, fluid dynamics, geophysics, physics, atmosphere, robotics, systems and control), electives, a case studies seminar, term project(s) and a 30-credit thesis. HPC is a skill inside simulation workflows, not the programme's identity; HPC-specific courses sit in D-INFK electives that were not enumerated in the guidelines.

programmes.notes: Read: the ETH study guidelines PDF (Feb 2025) and the programme page. The ETH course catalogue (vvz) and the Advanced Systems Lab course site (acl.inf.ethz.ch) were unreachable, so course descriptions are not verified; topic_coverage is null wherever the guidelines do not name a course. HPC electives from D-INFK (e.g. parallel programming) are plausible but were not found in the guidelines. No machine access (CSCS/Alps) is stated on the pages read; therefore machines_access is empty rather than assumed. The programme page (90 ECTS) and guidelines (120 ECTS) disagree: guidelines say students who started before or in spring 2024 follow the older 90-ECTS rules.
programmes.structure_summary_fr: Master interdisciplinaire en science et ingénierie computationnelles : deux cours de base choisis dans une liste (IA en sciences et ingénierie, apprentissage automatique avancé, méthodes numériques avancées, IA probabiliste, statistique computationnelle, laboratoire de systèmes avancés, optimisation pour la science des données), au moins deux domaines d'application (astrophysique, biologie, chimie, finance, électromagnétisme, dynamique des fluides, géophysique, physique, atmosphère, robotique, systèmes et contrôle), des options, un séminaire d'études de cas, un ou plusieurs projets et un mémoire de 30 crédits. Le HPC est une compétence au sein des chaînes de simulation, pas l'identité du programme ; les cours spécifiquement HPC se trouvent dans des options du département d'informatique que les directives n'énumèrent pas.
